衝.meaning: At a <part>crossroads</part> on a farm, two snails race from opposite lanes, each dragging a <part>heavy</part> shell piled high with luggage. Neither will slow down or step aside. Three days later, with a tiny click, they <kanji>collide</kanji>.
衝.on: A crowd of beetles bought tickets to watch the slow-motion <sound>show</sound>.
衝.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' hisses the slower snail, and jabs the other with a <sound>coo</sound>k's wooden spoon: to thrust.

潮.meaning: Every <part>morning</part> a crab sets up a deckchair at the very edge of the sand. By noon the <part>water drops</part> lap at its claws, then its knees, so it drags the chair back a few steps, grumbling. The crab never wins against the <kanji>tide</kanji>.
潮.on: As the sea rises, a wave snatches the crab's pearl <sound>cho</sound>ker and carries it away.
潮.kun: '<sound>She</sound> took my pearls! <sound>Oh</sound>!' wails the crab, shaking a claw at the sea.

岐.meaning: Halfway up a <part>mountain</part>, a hiker reaches a spot where the trail splits like a <part>branch</part>: left to a waterfall, right to a café. She flips a pancake to decide, and it lands on her head. Every good hike has a place where the path must <kanji>branch off</kanji>.
岐.on: On the signpost at the fork hangs a brass <sound>key</sound>, labelled 'For whichever way you pick.'

虐.meaning: A <part>tiger</part> crowns himself boss of the toy box. He makes the teddy bears line up by height, locks the crayons in a <part>drawer</part> and roars at any doll caught smiling. The toys whisper about a revolt. He loves to <kanji>tyrannize</kanji>.
虐.on: At night the toys slip a le<sound>ggy</sound>, <sound>yu</sound>cky rubber spider into the tiger's <sound>coo</sound>kie jar.
虐.kun: He even orders a toy <sound>shee</sound>p to fetch him a <sound>ta</sound>co every hour.

誇.meaning: At the pet show, a goldfish hires a <part>showman</part> to give a <part>speech</part> about him: 'He swam round this bowl ten thousand times! He once scared a cat!' The goldfish puffs up so much he floats to the top. He does love to <kanji>boast</kanji>.
誇.on: In the next cage, a sleepy <sound>ko</sound>ala yawns through the whole speech.
誇.kun: A parrot in the crowd heckles: '<sound>Ho</sound>, <sound>co</sound>ld fish, sit down!'

驚.meaning: A carousel <part>horse</part> stuck on its pole for fifty years is finally set free. It trots out of the fairground and freezes in <part>awe</part> at its first real meadow, its first cow, its first puddle. Every single thing is a <kanji>wonder</kanji>.
驚.on: A lost tourist holds up her map. '<sound>Kyo</sound>to?' she asks, stretching out the start, and the horse gapes at the map too.
驚.kun: An <sound>o</sound>tter, a <sound>do</sound>lphin and a <sound>ro</sound>bin rush over to meet the amazed horse and bring it a <sound>coo</sound>kie.
